Demonstrated ability to apply process-improvement methods to evaluate workflows, identify opportunities, implement sustainable improvements, and measure results. Lean Six Sigma Green Belt certification is preferred; training will be provided.

The University of California, Office of the President, is required to provide a reasonable estimate of the compensation range for this role. This range takes into account the wide range of factors that are considered in making compensation decisions including but not limited to experience, skills, knowledge, abilities, education, licensure and certifications, and other business and organizational needs. It is not typical for an individual to be offered a salary at or near the top of the range for a position. Salary offers are determined based on final candidate qualifications and experience. The full salary range shows the growth potential for this position and the pay scale is the budgeted salary or hourly range that the University reasonably expects to pay for this position.
Bachelor's degree in related area and / or equivalent experience / training

8 years experience, with a minimum of 3 years demonstrated experience overseeing and/or serving as a functional expert for accounts payable and/or purchasing, compliance, accounting, audit, or policy actions and activities, including at least 3 years of supervisory experience.
$131,000 - $150,000, Commensurate with Experience

Under general direction, the Manager of the Payables, Supplier, and Tax Services Team establishes goals, priorities, procedures, service standards, controls, and performance measures for accounts payable, supplier onboarding and maintenance, supplier tax services, and cash management. The manager achieves objectives through subordinate professional and administrative staff and is accountable for staffing, workload, quality, productivity, client service, compliance, and stewardship of University resources. The position provides operational leadership and subject-matter expertise for accounts payable, supplier onboarding and data maintenance, supplier tax services, and cash management functions. The manager ensures accurate financial transactions and supplier data, timely payments and tax reporting, compliance with applicable requirements, and effective controls to protect University resources and reduce supplier, payment, and tax-related fraud risk.  Please note this is a Hybrid position with three (3) days a week in Oakland, CA.

35% Operational Excellence, Service Delivery and People Management - Provide direction and expertise for accounts payable, supplier onboarding and maintenance, supplier tax services, and cash management. Translate BRC objectives into functional priorities, service standards, work plans, key performance indicators, quality measures, and measurable outcomes. Establish and promote a culture of operational excellence, accountability, continuous learning, innovation, and excellent customer service throughout the team. Directly manage professional and administrative staff. Assign and balance work, set clear service and performance expectations, monitor quality and productivity, provide timely feedback, coach and develop employees, support succession planning and employee engagement, and complete recruitment and performance-management activities. Hold staff accountable for operational results, service standards, internal controls, and professional growth. Determine how resources are used to meet schedules, transaction volumes, service commitments, and changing priorities. Monitor workload, accuracy, turnaround times, backlogs, escalations, quality, and client experience. Use operational, financial, workload, and service metrics to identify risks, address performance gaps, and improve outcomes. Report to BRC leadership regarding progress, resource needs, risks, controls, training, service levels, and performance measures. Foster collaboration across BRC teams, UCOP departments, systemwide partners, and external stakeholders to resolve service issues and improve end-to-end service delivery.

20% Accounts Payable, Disbursements and Cash Management - Direct timely, accurate, and policy-compliant invoice and payment processing, reconciliations, issue resolution, and customer service. Direct daily, weekly, monthly, period-close, and year-end reconciliation, monitoring, control, and reporting for PCard, ACH, checks, PaymentPlus, foreign wire transactions, fees, rebates, and related cash transactions. Oversee stale-dated checks, duplicate or misapplied payments, reissuance of expired payments, zero-dollar transactions, Positive Pay, federal and non-federal escheatment accounts, and month-end ARCS reporting and audit support.

20% Supplier Onboarding, Tax Services and Fraud Prevention - Direct onboarding, validation, maintenance, and customer service for all UCOP suppliers, and approve new supplier records and supplier banking changes. Ensure accurate supplier identity, banking, payment, classification, address, and tax data. Lead periodic and risk-based reviews to prevent supplier and payment fraud. Oversee tax-document review, withholding support, and annual Form 1099 and Form 1042 preparation, including nonresident and foreign supplier tax review with systemwide tax experts.

25% Continuous Improvement, Compliance, Internal Controls and Analysis - Develop, recommend, implement, document, and maintain procedures and controls for assigned services. Establish, assess, and strengthen internal controls that protect University resources. Coordinate analysis, dashboards, audit support, training, technology enhancements, automation, and process redesign.
Financial Services Manager 1
Benefits: For information on the comprehensive benefits package offered by the University visit: Benefits of Belonging
Advanced knowledge of applicable laws, interpretations, and industry best practices.
Knowledge of UC systems, processes and procedures, and rules and regulations.
Familiarity with, or demonstrated ability to learn, systems and programs used by BRC and its constituencies, including ServiceNow or another service management system.
Thorough knowledge of accounting and financial reporting concepts and related policy, accounting, and regulatory compliance requirements.
Ability to research and analyze financial transactions and balances.
Thorough knowledge of financial transactions and financial systems.
Demonstrated ability to understand and advise others regarding complex financial transactions, with excellent attention to detail and a high degree of accuracy.
Excellent interpersonal, oral, and written communication skills; strong service orientation; professional demeanor; and ability to interact with others in a direct, cooperative, and tactful manner.
Ability to multitask effectively in a varied, fast-paced, high-volume environment using sound judgment, decision-making, and reasoning.
Strong ability to collaborate effectively across UCOP to develop and achieve strategic goals.
